previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of gastroparesis was admitted for recurrent nausea and vomiting that began after taking morning medications on an empty stomach. She had no abdominal pain or signs of infection, and labs showed no metabolic derangement. Her symptoms improved with bowel rest, IV fluids, and symptom management. The hospital course was complicated by hypoglycemia due to reduced oral intake, prompting a temporary reduction in her evening Lantus insulin from 28 to 24 units. She gradually advanced to a regular diet, remained nausea-free, and was discharged home with instructions to resume her normal insulin dose when eating normally and to follow up with her primary care provider.

___ F with a history of DM1 who has frequent admissions for

# Nausea, vomiting: our patient was unable to tolerate PO at the 
time of admission, and had a witnessed small-volume episode of 
hematemesis felt secondary to ___ tear.  Aspirin was 
held in the context of hematemesis.  A KUB was unremarkable.  
LFTs and lipase were unremarkable.  All gastroparesis studies 
have been negative to date.  GI contacted the primary team on 
HD2 and expressed an interest in doing an EGD.  The patient 
underwent EGD, which revealed mid-esophageal varices and a 
stable area of patchiness in the stomach.  Ms. ___ HCT 
remained stable throughout admission, her nausea was treated 
with IV Zofran, and abdominal pain was treated with Dilaudid 
(not pushed).  She was kept NPO initially, but her diet was 
advanced as tolerated.  On the day of discharge, she had no 
abdominal pain, no nausea, and was tolerating full liquids 
without difficulty.  Ms. ___ should have outpatient 
evaluation of her varices, as she has no know history of liver 
disease, and the varices are of unclear etiology.  Please also 
discuss restarting her aspirin with her.

# GERD/esophagitis: since Ms. ___ symptoms could have been 
attributed to GERD and esophagitis, she was initially started on 
Pantoprazole IV.  However, once her EGD was done and there was 
no evidence of gastritis, esophagitis, or ulcerations, she was 
transitioned to her oral PPI.  

# Hypertension: Ms. ___ was noted to have elevated blood 
pressure in association with episodes of emesis, and it was 
initially felt that the two were related.  However, after 
patient's last episode of emesis, her blood pressures were still 
elevated (both systolic and diastolic). She was started on 
Lisinopril and titrated to a dose of 10mg daily.  At the time of 
discharge, her blood pressures ranged 100-116/70-88. 
  
# Chronic pain s/p MVA: Ms. ___ was given IV Dilaudid 
(diluted in 50cc of NS and hung over 15min) while not able to 
tolerate PO intake, but once able to tolerate PO, she was 
transitioned to her home dose of Tramadol.

# Diabetes Type I: Ms. ___ was continued on her home regimen 
of insulin (Lantus 28units qHS + ISS).  Her fingerstick glucose 
was occasionally elevated, however, it was also noted that the 
patient had many dietary indiscretions with concentrated sweets. 
 Ms. ___ was given diabetes nutrition counseling.  
  
# Psych: continued zoloft 50mg daily and ativan 1mg PO q6 PRN.  
Our patient was also followed by social work.
